cells.act: refine one distinction by close attention
cells.ask: There's a call in this work you make by feel — the pass that's ready against the one that's only lucky. Stay with that distinction for a week until you can describe what separates them.
cells.core:
The work is in your hands, and you aren't forcing it. Sessions run long because you want them to, and being alone with it has stopped feeling like being stuck. When you put something down, you know why you put it down. That's the tell: nothing has to be pried out of you, and the day's work is still there when you come back to it.

The next step is sharper seeing, not more hours. Somewhere in the work there's a judgment you make by feel — a difference you'd struggle to put into words. Give that difference your close attention for a week and leave the rest of the practice as it is. What you can name, you can build on. What stays blurry keeps costing you, quietly, each time you make that call again.

cells.tense: You will be ready once the work is deeper, and you're already bracing.
cells.act: mark the good thing together, out loud
cells.ask: Say what's genuinely good about the work as it stands now, to someone who knows what it costs — plainly, without adding what's still missing from it.
cells.core:
The next version of the work has taken over the present one. You're rehearsing a depth you haven't reached yet, and the pass under your hands keeps getting measured against a pass that doesn't exist. The pushing is real, and so is the skill — it's just aimed past everything you can touch. What's already built doesn't count much in your own accounting, and the hours keep going into a version of the work nobody can see yet.

Depth comes from repetition, and repetition needs something to keep it warm. So before the next stretch, say one true good thing about the work as it stands, to someone who knows what it takes. Not a progress report — the good part, named, with another person hearing it. The work keeps its weight. It also gets to be shared while it's still being made.

cells.tense: You stopped at a door that has already opened behind you.
cells.act: state the order of things once, without argument
cells.ask: Put the shape of your next stretch on paper — what you're doing, in what order, for how long — and hand it over as a statement, with no case made for it.
cells.core:
The practice is still there, and you're standing outside it. What you knew about the work — how to start, what order the day goes in, what a good session looks like — isn't in your hands right now. You watch it from a short distance, and the watching is easy to mistake for rest. Nothing in you reaches for the tools. This isn't about how good you are; it's that the door you're braced against already swung.

So put the frame where you can see it. Set down the shape of the next stretch — what you're doing, in what order, for how long — plainly, once, without arguing for it. No defence, no explanation of why it's the right call. It doesn't have to be the right frame, just a clear one, and a clear frame looks more like the work than the waiting does.

cells.tense: The pen is down on a page that is still being written.
cells.act: move at the pace your feeling can sustain
cells.ask: Set how much you'll take on next by what you can hold for a month, not a day — and when you catch yourself rushing to make up lost ground, slow to the pace you were keeping.
cells.core:
Something keeps the practice turning, and you'd call it habit. The deciding has a hand in it, and that hand is yours. The days you show up are days you chose, and the rhythm you keep wasn't handed to you — it came out of what you wanted, wearing the plain clothes of routine. The proof is that when the rhythm breaks, you notice before you can explain it.

So let what you want back into the steering. Set the size of the next stretch by what you can honestly keep for a month, not by what the schedule can argue. When you notice yourself speeding up to make up lost ground, ease off to the pace you were keeping. No announcement, no speech about it — just the pace and the want moving the same direction, and the momentum staying level instead of spiking.

attempts.check: The record can't say the person builds this alone or by hand on hard material — 'craft' is the mechanism's word, not theirs. A reader could object that their version of deep work is raising kids or holding a team together, not a bench, so the cells keep it to whatever the practice actually is. The asks survive being wrong: each one describes something they can do in whatever form the work takes, and none depends on my read being right. The sentence that serves me more than them is 'each pass deeper than the last' — it sounds like the record and would flatter the writer, so it stays out.

The sentence that serves me more than them is a line about mastery arriving at a threshold — it flatters the writer and tells the person nothing they can use, so it stays out.
